measures.id: City of Charlotte Transportation Bonds Referendum
measures.title: City of Charlotte Transportation Bonds
measures.summary: Asks whether the City of Charlotte may borrow up to $280,000,000 by issuing bonds to pay for street, road, intersection, sidewalk, bike and pedestrian path, bridge, storm drainage and related transportation improvements. The official ballot statement estimates the total cost over the life of the bonds at $437,113,600 ($280,000,000 principal plus $157,113,600 interest) and estimates the property tax increase needed to repay them at $0.00 per year per $100,000 of property value. If approved, the city may levy additional property taxes in an amount sufficient to pay the principal and interest.
measures.yesMeans: The City of Charlotte may issue up to $280,000,000 in bonds for street, road, intersection, sidewalk, bike and pedestrian path, bridge, storm drainage and related transportation improvements, and may levy property taxes sufficient to repay them.
measures.noMeans: The City of Charlotte may not issue these $280,000,000 in bonds.

measures.id: City of Charlotte Housing Bonds Referendum
measures.title: City of Charlotte Housing Bonds
measures.summary: Asks whether the City of Charlotte may borrow up to $125,000,000 by issuing bonds to pay for housing projects for people with low or moderate incomes, including related infrastructure and land. The official ballot statement estimates the total cost over the life of the bonds at $198,396,312.50 ($125,000,000 principal plus $73,396,312.50 interest) and estimates the property tax increase needed to repay them at $0.00 per year per $100,000 of property value. If approved, the city may levy additional property taxes in an amount sufficient to pay the principal and interest.
measures.yesMeans: The City of Charlotte may issue up to $125,000,000 in bonds for housing projects for people with low or moderate incomes, including related infrastructure and land, and may levy property taxes sufficient to repay them.
measures.noMeans: The City of Charlotte may not issue these $125,000,000 in bonds.

measures.id: City of Charlotte Neighborhood Improvement Bonds Referendum
measures.title: City of Charlotte Neighborhood Improvement Bonds
measures.summary: Asks whether the City of Charlotte may borrow up to $20,000,000 by issuing bonds to pay for neighborhood infrastructure such as curbs, gutters, storm drainage, sidewalks, bike and pedestrian paths, street resurfacing, lighting and public open space. The official ballot statement estimates the total cost over the life of the bonds at $31,222,400 ($20,000,000 principal plus $11,222,400 interest) and estimates the property tax increase needed to repay them at $0.00 per year per $100,000 of property value. If approved, the city may levy additional property taxes in an amount sufficient to pay the principal and interest.
measures.yesMeans: The City of Charlotte may issue up to $20,000,000 in bonds for neighborhood infrastructure such as curbs, gutters, storm drainage, sidewalks, bike and pedestrian paths, street resurfacing, lighting and public open space, and may levy property taxes sufficient to repay them.
measures.noMeans: The City of Charlotte may not issue these $20,000,000 in bonds.
